concrete.metaTitle: Concrete Calculator: Cubic Yards, m³ & Bags | BuildCalc
concrete.metaDescription: Calculate concrete volume for slabs, footings and columns in cubic yards or m³, with waste and the number of pre-mix bags. Free, with formulas explained.
concrete.intro: Find out how many cubic yards or cubic metres of concrete you need for a slab, footing, sidewalk or column, and how many bags of pre-mix to buy.

formula.title: How concrete is calculated
formula.p1: The volume of a rectangular slab or footing is the product of its three dimensions: V = length × width × thickness. For a round column we use the cylinder volume: V = π × r² × h, where r is half the diameter.
formula.p2: All measurements are first converted to metres (1 ft = 0.3048 m; 1 in = 0.0254 m), so the internal volume is always in m³. It is then displayed in cubic yards or m³ (1 yd³ = 0.7646 m³).
formula.p3: Waste is added as a percentage of the net volume. 5–10% covers concrete left in the mixer, uneven sub-grade and formwork deflection.
formula.p4: For bags we use the industry rule of thumb: an 80 lb bag yields ≈ 0.60 ft³ (≈ 45 bags per cubic yard). The same yield per kilogram is applied to 25, 40 and 50 kg bags (≈ 2136 kg of dry mix per m³). Always check the yield stated by the manufacturer.

faq.q: How many bags of concrete do I need for 1 cubic yard?
faq.a: About 45 bags of 80 lb or 60 bags of 60 lb per cubic yard. In metric, 1 m³ takes roughly 43 bags of 50 kg, 54 of 40 kg or 86 of 25 kg.

faq.q: What waste percentage should I use?
faq.a: 5% is usually enough for slabs on a well-levelled base; use 10% for hand-dug footings or small pours.

faq.q: Is thickness entered in inches or feet?
faq.a: In imperial the thickness is entered in inches (e.g. 4 in) and in metric in centimetres; the calculator converts automatically.

faq.q: Can I use this to order ready-mix from a truck?
faq.a: Yes. The total volume with waste is the amount to order; plants usually sell in increments of 0.25 yd³ or 0.5 m³.

paint.metaTitle: Paint Calculator: Gallons or Litres per Room | BuildCalc
paint.metaDescription: Calculate how much paint you need for walls and ceilings in gallons or litres. Subtract doors and windows, set coats, coverage and waste. Free and accurate.
paint.intro: Find out how many gallons or litres of paint to buy for a room, subtracting doors and windows and adjusting the number of coats and your paint's coverage.

fields.coverageHelp: Printed on the can. Typical: 300–400 ft²/gal (8–12 m²/L) per coat.

results.openingsWarning: Openings exceed the given area: check your measurements.

formula.title: How paint is calculated
formula.p1: First we get the wall area: perimeter × height = 2 × (length + width) × height. If you tick the ceiling, length × width is added.
formula.p2: We subtract openings using typical sizes: 20 ft² (1.9 m²) per door and 16 ft² (1.5 m²) per window. The result is the net area to paint.
formula.p3: The net area is multiplied by the number of coats and divided by the paint coverage (ft² per gallon or m² per litre) stated by the manufacturer.
formula.p4: Finally waste is added and the total is rounded up to whole containers of the chosen size. Rough or very absorbent surfaces may need up to 20% more.

faq.q: How much paint do I need for a 12 × 10 ft room?
faq.a: With 8 ft ceilings the walls are 352 ft²; after one door and one window about 316 ft² remain. Two coats at 350 ft²/gal need ≈ 1.8 gal, so two 1-gallon cans.

faq.q: How many coats of paint should I apply?
faq.a: Two coats is the standard for an even finish. Over dark colours or new drywall you may need three, or a coat of primer.
Most latex and acrylic paints cover 300–400 ft² per gallon per coat (8–12 m² per litre). The exact figure is printed on the can.

faq.q: Does the calculator work for exteriors?
faq.a: Yes: use the “Area already known” mode with the façade surface and raise waste to 10–15% for textured stucco or siding.

flooring.metaTitle: Flooring Calculator: Tiles, Boxes & Waste | BuildCalc
flooring.metaDescription: Calculate floor area in ft² or m², how many tiles or planks you need and the number of boxes, including cutting waste. Free and instant.
flooring.intro: Work out your floor area, the number of tiles, porcelain, laminate or vinyl planks and how many boxes to buy, with the right waste allowance for cuts.

fields.tileHelp: Tile or plank size. Leave empty if you only need the area.

formula.title: How flooring is calculated
formula.p1: The area of a rectangular room is length × width. For L-shaped or irregular rooms, split them into rectangles, add the areas and use the “Area already known” mode.
formula.p2: Waste covers cuts at edges, corners and around obstacles. We recommend 10% for straight layouts, 15% for diagonal or patterned layouts (herringbone, modular) and 5% for large simple rooms.
formula.p3: The number of pieces is the area to buy divided by the area of one piece (length × width), rounded up. Inch or centimetre sizes are converted automatically.
formula.p4: Boxes are the pieces divided by the box contents, or the area to buy divided by the ft² (m²) one box covers, always rounded up. Buy one spare box from the same batch for future repairs.

faq.q: How many 12 × 24 in tiles do I need for 120 ft²?
faq.a: Each tile covers 2 ft². With 10% waste the area to buy is 132 ft² → 66 tiles; with 8 tiles per box, 9 boxes.

faq.q: How much waste should I allow for laminate or vinyl plank?
faq.a: 7–10% for straight layouts. If the room has many corners or you lay diagonally, go up to 15%.

faq.q: Should I subtract furniture or kitchen cabinets?
faq.a: Not movable furniture. You can subtract kitchen islands or permanent built-ins using the “Area already known” mode.

faq.q: Does the calculator account for grout joints?
faq.a: No: the grout gap (1/16–3/16 in) adds a small margin in your favour that is already covered by the waste percentage.

privacy.metaDescription: BuildCalc privacy policy covering calculator inputs, local storage, technical data, cookies, analytics, advertising and affiliate links.

sections.title: 1. Who we are
sections.text: BuildCalc is a free website offering construction calculators and tools in Spanish and English. This policy explains what information may be processed when you use the website.

sections.title: 2. Information entered into calculators
sections.text: Calculations are performed directly in your browser. Measurements, quantities and other values you enter are not deliberately sent to our servers or stored in a user account. Registration is not required to use the tools.

sections.title: 3. Local storage
sections.text: The website may save preferences, such as your selected measurement system, in your browser's local storage. This information remains on your device and can be deleted through your browser settings by clearing the website's data.

sections.title: 4. Technical information
sections.text: The hosting provider may automatically log technical information required to deliver and protect the website, such as IP address, access date and time, requested pages, browser, operating system, device and referring page. The processing of these logs is also subject to the provider's policies.

sections.title: 5. Cookies and similar technologies
sections.text: BuildCalc uses local storage for certain preferences. Local storage is not the same as a cookie. Google Analytics and Google AdSense advertising are currently disabled. If we introduce cookies or other tracking technologies in the future, we will update this policy and apply the relevant information and consent mechanisms.

sections.title: 6. Analytics
sections.text: Google Analytics is not currently enabled on BuildCalc. If we introduce measurement tools in the future, we may collect usage statistics such as pages visited, device type and approximate location, according to the provider's settings and policies.

sections.title: 7. Advertising and affiliate links
sections.text: Advertising and affiliate links are currently disabled. In the future, the website may display third-party advertisements or clearly identified affiliate links. BuildCalc may earn a commission if you make a purchase through an affiliate link, at no additional cost to you. External providers may use cookies or other technologies according to their own policies.

sections.title: 8. Sharing information
sections.text: We do not sell or rent personal information. Technical information may be processed by hosting and security providers to maintain the website. Any external service introduced in the future will also be subject to its own terms and privacy policies.

sections.title: 9. Links to external websites
sections.text: BuildCalc may contain links to other websites. We do not control their content, privacy practices or security measures. We recommend reviewing their policies before providing any personal information.

sections.title: 10. Data retention and security
sections.text: Preferences stored locally remain on your device until you delete them. Technical hosting logs are retained according to the provider's terms. We apply reasonable measures to keep the website secure, although no system can guarantee absolute security.

sections.title: 11. Children's privacy
sections.text: BuildCalc is not designed to deliberately collect personal information from children. No account or personal information is required to use its calculators.

sections.title: 12. Your rights and questions
sections.text: Depending on applicable law, you may have the right to request access to, correction, updating or deletion of your personal information. For privacy questions, you can contact the project through GitHub Issues: https://github.com/resktoff/Buildcalc-/issues. Please note that comments posted there may be publicly visible. Do not share sensitive information in an issue.

sections.title: 13. Changes to this policy
sections.text: We may update this policy when website features, services or legal requirements change. The update date will appear at the beginning of this page.

sections.title: 14. Scope of this information
sections.text: This policy provides general information about how BuildCalc works and does not constitute legal advice. If the website introduces new services or begins processing personal information in other ways, we will review this policy and the applicable obligations.
